issue.title: Security vulnerability: golang.org/x/net (CVE-2026-39821, CVE-2026-46600) bundled in v2.97.0
issue.body:
### Description

We ran a Trivy scan on our own Docker image and it flagged two vulnerabilities in golang.org/x/net, bundled inside the pre built gh binary (v2.97.0, built with go1.26.5).

CVE-2026-39821 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5026): a Punycode decoding bug in golang.org/x/net/idna. Fixed in net/http at go1.26.6.

We ran govulncheck against the v2.97.0 source and it confirms this one is reachable through gh's own code, through normal HTTP client calls. A few of the traces it found:

pkg/cmd/agent-task/capi/sessions.go:390:29: capi.CAPIClient.ListSessionsByResourceID calls http.Client.Do 
pkg/cmd/copilot/copilot.go:284:29: copilot.downloadCopilot calls http.Client.Get 
api/queries_repo.go:1679:33: api.RepoExists calls http.Client.Head 
internal/authflow/flow.go:95:31: authflow.AuthFlow calls oauth.Flow.DetectFlow, which eventually calls http.Client.PostForm

CVE-2026-46600 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5942): a DNS record parsing bug in golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage. Fixed in net at go1.26.6.

govulncheck shows the net package is linked in, but it did not find a call chain into the vulnerable function specifically, so I cannot show this one is reachable the same way. Listing it here since it is bundled in the same binary and fixed by the same toolchain bump.

### Purpose

Both are fixed by moving to a Go toolchain at go1.26.6 or newer. Could a future gh release be built with that? That would clear both for downstream Docker image scans.
